description:
FILED s470bi (Opus, 2026-09-05) with #1020's fix.  The RESIDUE #1020 does not
close, and the reason perl-tests/sub.t row 24 stays failing.

#1020 makes `undef *GLOB` clear every slot, so every VALUE spelling now
matches perl (`defined $s`, `@a`, `%h`, `defined &c`, `exists &c`, `print FH`).
The INTROSPECTION spelling still diverges, because perl REMOVES the aggregate
slot where PCL empties it.

MEASURED, perl 5.40.3 (scratch/s470bi/p1020/slots2.pl -- ORDER MATTERS, a read
of @a re-vivifies its slot, which is why the first probe of this looked like
agreement):

    our $s = 5; our @a = (9); our %h = (k=>1); sub c { "code" }
    undef *s; undef *a; undef *h; undef *c;
    # BEFORE touching any of them:
    *s{SCALAR}  def          *a{ARRAY}  undef
    *h{HASH}    undef        *c{CODE}   undef
    # then, after `@a ? ... : ...` has READ @a:
    *a{ARRAY}   def          (perl re-vivified it on the read)

PCL after #1020: SCALAR def (correct), ARRAY/HASH **def** (a fresh empty
container), CODE undef (correct).

WHY #1020 DID NOT TAKE IT: `makunbound` on the aggregate slot symbols was
tried and REVERTED (measured, s469bi).  It gives the right `*a{ARRAY}` AND
`push @a, 42` still works (it re-vivifies, matching perl exactly) -- but a
plain READ (`@a ? ... : ...`) CRASHES on the unbound symbol-macro cell.  So
the slot cannot simply go away without VIVIFY-ON-READ for package aggregates,
which is a change to every aggregate read in the runtime.  #602's rule
(`%p-glob-empty-slot`) is what #1020 ships instead.

THE ROW IT OWNS: perl-tests/sub.t row 24 `goto &xsub when @_ does not exist`
(`undef *_; eval { &utf8::encode }; is *_{ARRAY}, undef`).  PCL answers an
array ref.  The row is in baselines/fail-baseline.tsv; its cause line was
#1020's and is RE-POINTED at this task, because #1020's own defect (a silent
no-op for every glob) is fixed and this one is not.  The same row is in the
companion t/op/sub.t inside its blessed count.

FIX SHAPE (untried): vivify-on-read for a package aggregate whose cell is
unbound -- then `%p-glob-clear-var-slot` can `makunbound` the `@`/`%` slots
instead of emptying them, and `*a{ARRAY}` answers undef until something reads
@a.  Cost: a boundp test on every package-aggregate read, so it needs the
bench (`tools/bench-exec.pl`) before it ships.


=== SIZED (s473h, Opus, 2026-09-08) â the three numbers the fix needs; NOT designed ===

The brief asked for the cheap discriminating measurement (CLAUDE.md's "suspect
X" rule) and nothing else.  Here it is.  Fable designs from it.

(i) HOW MANY READ SITES DOES THE EMISSION HAVE?
    A package aggregate is `(p-defcell @a â¦)`, i.e.
    `(define-symbol-macro @a (sb-ext:symbol-global-value '@a))` â so EVERY
    occurrence of the bare symbol, read AND write, is one expansion of the
    cell access, and a vivify-on-read guard sits in that ONE expansion.
    Counted over the emitted CL of 40 perl-tests files (the tool is
    scratch/s473h/count-agg.pl: strip CL string literals, find the
    p-defcell/defvar names, count their other occurrences):

        files  1-20:   87 package aggregates,  713 sites,  11 317 CL lines
        files 21-40:   58 package aggregates,  494 sites,   8 469 CL lines
        ------------------------------------------------------------------
        total:        145 aggregates,        1 207 sites,  19 786 CL lines

    ~6 % of emitted lines carry one.  Per file the spread is wide: array.t
    294 sites, closure.t 88, and 12 of the 40 files have none at all.

(ii) WHAT WOULD VIVIFY-ON-READ COST?
    Hand-built, exactly as the brief asked: ONE emitted file with each
    aggregate's `p-defcell` replaced by

        (define-symbol-macro @a
          (or (and (boundp '@a) (sb-ext:symbol-global-value '@a))
              (setf (sb-ext:symbol-global-value '@a) (make-array 0 â¦))))

    (scratch/s473h/agg2-base.lisp vs agg2-viv.lisp, both from
    scratch/s473h/probe/aggbench2.pl).  The program is a loop that does
    NOTHING BUT package-aggregate element access â `$a[$i % 1000]`,
    `$h{$i % 100}`, `$a[7] = $i`, `$a[7]` â so this is an UPPER BOUND, not a
    typical cost.  Interleaved best-of-7 with the bench-exec subtraction
    (t(N=30 000 000) â t(N=0), so startup and load cancel):

        run 1:  base 1.6429 s   viv 1.6972 s   ratio 1.033
        run 2:  base 1.6557 s   viv 1.7425 s   ratio 1.053

    So **3â5 % on a loop made entirely of these accesses**.  CAVEAT, stated
    because the rule requires it: `uptime` showed load 4.2â4.8 throughout (a
    sibling agent was running), so treat 5 % as the pessimistic end.

    THE STRUCTURAL FINDING BEHIND THAT NUMBER, and it is the useful half:
    **a foreach over the aggregate expands the cell ONCE, not per element.**
    `for my $x (@a)` lowers to `(p-foreach-raw ($x @a) â¦)`, which evaluates
    `@a` once and then iterates the vector â so the guard is invisible there.
    The cost lands only on per-ELEMENT sites (`$a[$i]`, `$h{$k}`) inside a
    loop, which is why the first bench I wrote (a foreach loop) measured NO
    difference at all and had to be replaced.

(iii) WHO CONSUMES `*a{ARRAY}` / `*a{HASH}` BESIDES PERL'S OWN t/?
    Grepped over all four populations:

        lib/               0 files
        cpan-tests/        1 real module â cpan-tests/modules/easy-targets/Carp.pm
                           (plus its two transpiled copies)
        perl-tests/        2 files â magic.t, sub.t
        Pl/t/              6 files (misc-fixes-01/-02, aassign-01,
                           glob-slot-operand-01, transpile-test-05,
                           glob-undef-01)
        perl's own t/      11 files

    Carp is the only NON-TEST consumer, and it uses the slot exactly as a
    GUARD, four times:

        return unless ref \$_ eq 'GLOB' && *$_{HASH} && exists $$_{$sub};   (:34)
        return 0 unless ref \$_ eq "GLOB" && *$_{HASH} && exists $$_{...};  (:122, :124)
        â¦ && *{$stash->{$var}}{ARRAY} && @{$stash->{$var}} â¦                (:736)

    Every one has a SECOND conjunct that re-tests the container's contents,
    so Carp survives PCL's always-"present" answer today.  That is the idiom
    #1242 gets wrong, and it is also why nothing has broken yet.

WHAT THE THREE NUMBERS SAY TOGETHER (an observation, not a design): the
guard's cost is concentrated in per-element access inside loops and is 0 for
the foreach shape, the site count is large but the HOT subset is not the same
set, and the only non-test consumer is guard-shaped.  A design that pays the
boundp only where the slot is actually introspected â rather than on every
cell expansion â would cost nothing measurable; whether that is expressible is
Fable's call.

STOP.  No fix attempted, per the brief.


=== DESIGN (s480, Fable, 2026-09-09) â from the s473h sizing; ONE USER DECISION open, then Opus ===

THE PROBE THAT CLOSED THE FREE-EXACT OPTION.  SBCL 2.6.0 offers NO per-variable
restart on an unbound global read: in both the evaluated and the COMPILED path
the restarts at the unbound-variable signal are the LOADER's (`RETRY` = "Retry
EVAL of current toplevel form", `CONTINUE` = "Ignore error and continue loading",
ABORT x2) â no use-value / store-value.  So a `makunbound` slot cannot be
re-vivified in place by a handler (scratch: unbound-restart2.lisp), and the
s469bi revert stands.  Vivify-on-read is therefore EITHER a per-site guard in
the symbol-macro expansion (the s473h number: 3â5 % on a loop that is nothing
but element access; 0 on foreach) OR not modelled.

TWO SHAPES; Fable RECOMMENDS (B).

(A) EXACT: `(define-symbol-macro @a (or (and (boundp '@a) (symbol-global-value '@a)) (%p-vivify-agg '@a)))`
    for every package aggregate; `%p-glob-clear-var-slot` makunbounds the @/% slot;
    `p-glob-slot` unchanged (boundp already answers).  Every read AND write site pays the
    guard (1207 sites / 40 files, s473h (i)); measured upper bound 1.033â1.053 on the
    element-access loop; `for my $x (@a)` unaffected (the cell is read once).  `&foo;`
    (the no-parens `&` call) must read @_ WITHOUT vivifying â perl passes the caller's
    @_ through GvAV, no GvAVn â or sub.t row 24 still fails under (A).

(B) ZERO-COST, one documented residue.  The cell stays BOUND to the fresh empty
    container `%p-glob-clear-var-slot` already installs; that container is registered in
    a weak-key `eq` table `*p-removed-agg-slots*` (`(make-hash-table :test 'eq :weakness :key)`).
    `p-glob-slot`'s ARRAY/HASH arms answer undef when the cell's container is IN the table
    AND STILL EMPTY (length 0 / hash-count 0); a non-empty one was written â `remhash`, answer
    the ref (a write vivifies, as in perl).  `*a = \@other` / `%p-glob-slot-place` install a
    DIFFERENT container, which is simply not in the table â nothing to clear.  No read or
    write path changes: the ONLY new instruction is one eq-hash lookup inside `*a{ARRAY}` /
    `*a{HASH}`.  RESIDUE (not modelled, goes in docs/not-supported.md as its own section with
    the probe): after `undef *a`, a READ of @a (`my @x = @a`, `@a ? 1 : 0`, `\@a`) or an
    EMPTY write (`@a = ()`, `$#a = -1`) re-vivifies the slot in perl, so `*a{ARRAY}` is then a
    ref in perl and still undef in PCL until something makes @a NON-EMPTY.  Population: perl's
    own t/ (11 files) + perl-tests magic.t/sub.t; Carp â the only non-test consumer â uses the
    slot as a GUARD (`*$_{HASH} && exists $$_{$sub}`), and under (B) the guard short-circuits
    exactly where perl's does (probe it in the batch: Carp's four sites on a glob whose hash
    slot was never created / was undef'd / was written).

WHY (B): Target A is absolute speed (USER 2026-09-05); (A) taxes the hottest emission shape
in the language for an introspection corner whose only consumers are perl's own tests, and
the residue under (B) is a documented, probe-named class, not a silent one.  (A) is the fallback
if the USER wants exactness at that price; nothing in (B) blocks moving to (A) later (the table
becomes dead code).

MEMBERS (Opus, one batch, ~S): 1. the table + the two `p-glob-slot` arms + `%p-glob-clear-var-slot`
registration (rule 11: ONE reading â `undef *G` and `*A = *B`'s clear half both go through it
already); 2. guard rows in `Pl/t/glob-undef-01.t` = the task's MEASURED table (before touching:
SCALAR def, ARRAY undef, HASH undef, CODE undef; after `push @a, 42` â def; after `%h = (k=>1)` â def;
`*a = \@o` â def AND `\@o == *a{ARRAY}`; `*a = *b` where b has no @ â undef; sub.t row 24's
own shape `undef *_; eval { &utf8::encode }; *_{ARRAY}`), inverse-verified; the not-supported
section with the residue probes (perl's answer beside PCL's); 3. `perl-tests/sub.t` row 24 leaves
`baselines/fail-baseline.tsv` by EDIT; companion `op/sub.t op/gv.t op/magic.t op/undef.t` `--jobs 1`
before/after, spliced by hand; `cl/` change â the full sweep (0 new / 0 LOST, TOTAL +1); ir-spec Â§7
(globs) gains the normative sentence: "an aggregate slot cleared by `undef *G` reads as ABSENT from
`*G{ARRAY}`/`*G{HASH}` until a write makes it non-empty; reads do not re-vivify (residue: not-supported
Â§<name>)"; `tools/ir-conform --jobs 2`.


=== RULED (USER, s484, 2026-09-13) â (B), with a STOP-RULE ===

USER: "OK, do (B).  But ignore this and document this, if it is expensive to
implement."

So: implement shape (B) exactly as designed above (the weak-key table, the two
`p-glob-slot` arms, registration in `%p-glob-clear-var-slot`; no read or write
path changes; the residue documented in docs/not-supported.md as its own
section with the probe table).

STOP-RULE (the USER's "if it is expensive"): the design is sized S â ONE Opus
batch, runtime-only, no emission change.  If the implementation turns out to
need (a) a change to any aggregate READ or WRITE path, (b) a generation bump,
(c) a new mechanism beyond the one eq-hash table, or (d) more than the batch's
session, then DO NOT SHIP THE FIX: revert it (save the diff in the batch's
scratch), and instead write the DIVERGENCE into docs/not-supported.md â the
measured table from the FILED section above (perl's answers beside PCL's,
before and after a read), sub.t row 24's cause line re-pointed at that section
(`NS:<section>`), and this task marked DONE (documented, not implemented).
Either outcome closes the task.


=== DONE (s484b, 2026-09-13, Opus) === IMPLEMENTED as shape (B).  The
STOP-RULE did NOT fire: no read or write path changed, no generation bump
(emission IDENTICAL over 111 files), no mechanism beyond the one weak `eq`
table, one batch.

THE MECHANISM (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp, 3 new forms + 2 edited arms):
  *p-removed-agg-slots*   weak-key `eq` set of the empty containers a glob
                          CLEAR installed
  %p-agg-slot-empty-p     rule-12 emptiness test over the two aggregate
                          representations (a third kind ERRORS)
  %p-agg-slot-cleared-p   in the set AND still empty; a container found
                          non-empty is remhash'd and answers PRESENT for good
  %p-glob-clear-var-slot  registers the empty for the "@" and "%" slots -- the
                          ONE place both clearing spellings meet (`undef *G`
                          and `*A = *B`'s missing-slot half; verified: that
                          helper has exactly two callers and %p-glob-empty-slot
                          exactly one)
  p-glob-slot             the ARRAY and HASH arms consult it

THE RULE: a cleared aggregate slot is ABSENT while its registered container is
EMPTY, and PRESENT from the first read that finds it non-empty.  EMPTY is not
ABSENT -- `our @o = ()` and `*a = \@other` have their slots.

MEASURED (perl 5.40.3 | PCL before | PCL after), scratch/s484b/probe/:
  after `undef *s *a *h *c`, nothing touched:
      SCALAR  def | def | def          ARRAY  undef | def | UNDEF
      HASH  undef | def | UNDEF        CODE   undef | undef | undef
  push @a,42 / %h=(k=>1)          def | def | def
  *a = \@o                        def + `== \@o` in all three
  *a2 = *b2 (b2 scalar-only)    undef | def | UNDEF
  never-created / scalar-only    undef | undef | undef
  double `undef *d`, then push   undef then def, in all three
  sub.t row 24's shape          undef | def | UNDEF
  our @o = () (never cleared)     def | def | def
  *c = \@empty_foreign            def | def | def
  glob-copy BOUND half, aliased-then-undef'd, hash copy, `push @{*e}`
                                  all four identical to perl before and after

RESIDUE, documented (docs/not-supported.md "`undef *GLOB` leaves an EMPTY
aggregate slot where perl REMOVES it", 12-row probe table; ir-spec Â§7.2
normative):
  (a) perl re-vivifies a cleared slot on ANY READ of @a (`my @x = @a`,
      `@a ? 1 : 0`, `\@a`, `keys %h`) and on an EMPTY write (`@a = ()`,
      `$#a = -1`); PCL does not.  Closing it is shape (A)'s 3-5 % guard.
  (b) PCL asks at READ time, so a write undone before anything asks
      (`push @a,42; pop @a`) reads ABSENT where perl has been present since
      the push; a read that DOES observe it non-empty deregisters it for good
      (probed: `push; *a{ARRAY}; pop; *a{ARRAY}` is present twice in both).
      Closing it is a hook in every aggregate write path = stop-rule (a).

BARS: gate 172/5786 PASS (only the 13 pclxs xs rows red, the standing state);
sweep `--jobs 4` GATE clean, 0 new / 0 fixed / 0 LOST, drops 5 = census,
TOTAL 18675 -> 18676 (the +1 IS sub.t row 24); ir-conform 323 pass / 0 fail /
22 known / 0 stale; ir-host-leak byte-identical to the base; corpus-diff
IDENTICAL over 111 files; tag-license clean.  Guard Pl/t/glob-undef-01.t
5 -> 9 rows (922 ms), rows 6/7/9 inverse-verified FAILING on an a217cb49
extraction.  No bench row: the emission is unchanged and the only new
instruction is one eq-hash lookup inside `*G{ARRAY}` / `*G{HASH}`.

BASELINES (row by row, with causes): perl-tests/sub.t row 24 out of
fail-baseline.tsv, pass-baseline.tsv sub.t 53 -> 54; companion op/sub.t
54/11 -> 55/10 in perl-suite-run.tsv and its row out of perl-suite-fails.tsv;
ir-conform/known-fail.tsv 077/078/092-typeglob OUT (they pass), 094-typeglob's
cause rewritten (it fails at its LAST line only now), 037-autoviv IN -- an
ACCIDENTAL pass this fix exposed (it asks the slots after a read, so perl says
def and PCL used to say def for the opposite reason).

FILED: #1726 (`exists $$_{k}` on a GLOB-valued $_ is false in PCL, true in
perl -- all four of Carp's guards short-circuit there, which is why (B)
changes none of Carp's answers), #1727 (`local *G` is a THIRD clear path,
%p-glob-clear, that registers nothing).
